subtopics.title: Where People Are — Distribution, Density and Why

questions.question: Population distribution and population density differ in that:
options: Distribution describes the pattern of where people are; density measures people per unit of area
Distribution is measured in people per square kilometre; density is a map pattern
They are two words for the same measurement
Density applies only to cities and distribution only to farms

questions.question: A district of 2 million people covering 40 000 square kilometres has a density of:
options: 500 people per square kilometre
50 people per square kilometre
5 people per square kilometre
200 people per square kilometre

questions.question: Gauteng became South Africa's densest concentration of people mainly because:
options: It has the country's highest rainfall
It lies on the coast with natural harbours
It has the most fertile soils in the country
The 1886 gold discoveries pulled labour, railways and industry onto the Highveld

questions.question: Egypt shows that national density figures can mislead because:
options: Its population is evenly spread across the desert
Its census is unreliable
Density is an average, and nearly everyone actually lives crowded along the Nile
Deserts always have high density

subtopics.title: Growth, Structure and the Population Pyramid

questions.question: A birth rate of 30 per thousand and a death rate of 10 per thousand give a natural increase of:
options: 40 per thousand, or 4 per cent
3 per cent
0.3 per cent
20 per thousand, or 2 per cent

questions.question: In stage two of the demographic transition model, population explodes because:
options: The death rate falls with clean water and vaccines while the birth rate stays high
Both birth and death rates rise together
The birth rate rises while the death rate is unchanged
Migration brings millions into the country

questions.question: A population pyramid with a wide base and a narrow top indicates:
options: Low birth rate and an ageing population
A high birth rate, a young fast-growing population and heavy youth dependency
A shrinking population with few children
Equal numbers in every age group

questions.question: Overpopulation is best defined as:
options: Any population above 100 million people
A density above 1 000 people per square kilometre
More people than an area's resources can support at an acceptable standard of living
A city with informal settlements

subtopics.title: People on the Move — Migration, Urbanisation and Settlement

questions.question: The same person leaving South Africa to settle in Australia is called:
options: An immigrant in South Africa and an emigrant in Australia
A refugee in both countries
A commuter between the two countries
An emigrant from South Africa and an immigrant in Australia

questions.question: Push factors driving rural-urban migration in South Africa include:
options: City jobs, schools and hospitals
Unemployment, drought and poor services in the sending regions
Bright lights and entertainment in cities
Remittances sent home by relatives

questions.question: Urbanisation is defined as:
options: The total number of people living in cities
The building of new towns by government
The rising percentage of a population living in towns and cities
The movement of people between two cities

questions.question: Informal settlements often occupy floodplains and steep slopes because:
options: That land is the unclaimed land left over near the jobs, which nobody else wanted
The views are better there
Government allocates that land first
Floodplains have the best building soil

subtopics.title: Water in a Dry Country — Floods and Water Management

questions.question: South Africa's average annual rainfall compared with the world average is roughly:
options: 464 millimetres against a world average near 860
860 millimetres against a world average of 464
Exactly equal to the world average
Double the world average

questions.question: The Lesotho Highlands Water Project is an example of:
options: A desalination plant on the coast
A groundwater borehole scheme
A flood-control wall around a city
An inter-basin transfer scheme moving mountain water to Gauteng

questions.question: On a flood hydrograph, an urbanised sealed catchment shows:
options: A long lag time and a low broad peak
A short lag time and a high narrow peak
No peak at all
A falling limb steeper than any rising limb

questions.question: The free basic water policy entitles every poor household to:
options: Unlimited free water
600 litres per month
6 000 litres per month
60 000 litres per month

questions.question: In the party picture, the crowded kitchen stands for:
options: Places like Gauteng where jobs concentrate people onto a small area
The empty arid west of the country
The whole of South Africa equally
Rural villages far from cities

questions.question: The Northern Cape is the party's cold stoep because:
options: It is too cold for settlement
Its aridity offers little farming and little work, leaving about 2 people per square kilometre
It has no roads at all
Government forbids settlement there

questions.question: When commenting on any density figure in an exam, the smart move is to:
options: Round it to the nearest hundred
Compare it only with Egypt
Convert it into a percentage
Ask how the people are actually spread inside that average

questions.question: The three glances for reading any population pyramid are:
options: The colours, the labels and the title
The base for births, the slope of the sides for survival, and the top for old age
The left side, the right side and the middle
The scale, the source and the year

questions.question: The column-shaped pyramid's new problem is:
options: Too many babies for the schools
High infant mortality
Too few workers supporting too many pensioners
Rapid population explosion

questions.question: The visible notch in South Africa's young-adult pyramid bars records:
options: The HIV and Aids pandemic's toll before the treatment programme turned life expectancy upward
Emigration of pensioners
A baby boom in the 1990s
An undercount in the census

subtopics.title: The Bucket with a Hole — South Africa's Water Story

questions.question: The bucket leaks refers to the fact that:
options: Dams evaporate completely every summer
Rivers flow backwards in drought
Rainfall drains into the sea unused
About a third of municipal water is lost through broken pipes and dripping taps

questions.question: A farmer switching to drip irrigation can save more water than many households because:
options: Households use no water at all
About two-thirds of South Africa's water goes to agriculture
Drip irrigation uses more water than flood irrigation
Farm water is free of charge

questions.question: Cape Town's Day Zero countdown in 2018 stands as a warning that:
options: Desalination always fails
Only coastal cities face water shortages
Water management is not optional even for a major city
Dams cause droughts

questions.question: The chain linking population, settlement and water in one story is:
options: People moved for work, settled on leftover land, and the leftover land was the flood-prone land the river claims
Floods cause migration to floodplains
Water attracts people away from jobs
Settlement patterns have no link to flooding
